ev.q: approximately 6.5 million topical antifungal prescriptions were filled (134 prescriptions per 1,000 beneficiaries), at a total cost of $231 million.
the highest prescription rate was in the Northeast (188.0 prescriptions per 1,000 beneficiaries), followed by the South (138.1 per 1,000).
The number of prescriptions per provider was highest for dermatologists (87.1), followed by podiatrists (67.2), and primary care physicians (12.3).
Among all topical antifungal prescriptions, 44.2% (2.9 million) were written by the top 10% (13,106) of topical antifungal prescribers.
The highest average per prescription costs were for efinaconazole ($1,035.38), tavaborole ($784.63), and oxiconazole ($729.84)
During 2021, a total of 6.5 million topical antifungal prescriptions were filled by Part D beneficiaries (overall rate = 134.0 prescriptions per 1,000 beneficiaries)
Total prescription volumes were compared between higher-volume prescribers (top 10% of topical antifungal prescribers by volume) and lower-volume prescribers.
By provider type, the percentage of topical antifungal prescriptions written by higher-volume topical antifungal prescribers ranged from 35.5% for dermatologists to 54.8% for podiatrists.
Most prescriptions were written by primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, or physician assistants.

equity.level_reason: Comparisons are by drug, provider type, region and prescriber volume, none of which is a social-position dimension; the population is Medicare Part D beneficiaries.

level_alternative.reason: Only if 'more ready access to medical care', offered for the Northeast's higher rate, were read as an equity framing; region is not an SPD.

equity.equity_measurement: Data are aggregated by prescriber and drug, with no patient-level age, sex, race or SES; regional differences only.

notes: No tests or CIs; all results are hand-computed rates, percentages and costs. The top-10% volume cutoff is quantization, not a procedure. Design inferred as surveillance/descriptive (secondary analysis of public CMS data); none is named. Age eligibility for Medicare appears only in a program-description footnote, so no age dimension is recorded; the enrollment dataset serves only as denominator.
view_issues: Data Analysis repeats itself ('were calculated by drug and region and to calculate prescription rates per 1,000 beneficiaries by drug and region'). Ketoconazole counts cannot separate oral from topical forms (Table 1 note).
